oewn-01446913-a.learner: Of a speech sound or syllable: lasting a fairly long time when you say it.
examples: The vowel sound in 'boot' is long, but the one in 'book' is short.

oewn-00015626-s.learner: Having more than the normal or needed amount, or being more than that amount.
examples: The team is long on talent but short on experience.

oewn-01901363-s.learner: Careful and wise in making plans for the future.
examples: She took a long view and saved money for her children's schooling.
He has a long memory and never forgets an unkind word.
He put his money on the horse at long odds.

oewn-01447325-a.learner: Holding shares or goods because you expect their prices to go up.
examples: The trader is long on coffee this season.

oewn-02730292-v.learner: To be in a relationship with someone or something.
examples: The parts of the machine relate to one another in a simple way.

oewn-02463535-v.learner: To have a relationship with someone or something, or to build one.
examples: The new teacher relates well to the younger children.

oewn-14035972-n.learner: A state of not moving or not doing anything.
examples: The ball stayed at rest until someone kicked it.

oewn-13986101-n.learner: Death, spoken of in a gentle way as if the dead person were lying asleep in a bed.
examples: The old soldier was laid to rest in the churchyard.

oewn-04088156-n.learner: Something that holds things up, which you can put things on.
examples: She set the gun on a rest to keep it steady.

oewn-06878227-n.learner: A sign in written music that shows a silence of a set length.
examples: There is a rest at the end of the second bar, so the singer stops for one beat.

oewn-05963348-n.learner: The ordered set of beliefs held by a person, a group, or a time in history.
examples: The book traces the growth of Greek thought.

oewn-06694296-n.learner: A short report of something in the news.
examples: The newspaper's account of the speech made the mayor angry.

oewn-13952070-n.learner: A formal arrangement with a bank or other business so that you can use its services regularly.
examples: She opened an account at the bank near her office.

oewn-06528946-n.learner: A list showing each item of money you owe for goods sent or work done.
examples: The shop sent an account listing everything we owed for the coal.

oewn-13376000-n.learner: A written record of recent payments in and out, and the amount of money left at the end.
examples: Each month the bank sends an account showing what came in, what went out, and the balance.
He was a man of little account in the town.

oewn-07232584-n.learner: The act of telling someone about something by giving a report in words.
examples: "I am very glad to hear such a good account of her," said Lady Catherine

oewn-05165115-n.learner: The state of using something in a way that gains you something.
examples: He put his years abroad to good account in his new job.

oewn-07307886-n.learner: The kind of treatment someone gets, especially because of an agreement.
examples: The farmers felt they were getting an unfair deal from the company.

oewn-01087261-n.learner: The act of handing out playing cards to the players.
examples: She shuffled the pack and began the deal.

oewn-07973501-n.learner: The cards that one player is holding at a given moment in a card game.
examples: He looked at his deal and knew he could not win the round.

oewn-01086561-n.learner: The act of sharing out or handing out something.
examples: The captain was put in charge of the deal of food to the crew.

oewn-15127189-n.learner: A board of soft wood, such as fir or pine.
examples: The floor was made of rough deals nailed side by side.

oewn-15124824-n.learner: Wood that is easy to saw, which comes from trees such as pine or fir.
examples: The kitchen table was made of plain deal.

oewn-00051015-n.learner: The act of coming out where the public can see you.
examples: The singer made her last appearance on stage in Paris.

oewn-05948150-n.learner: A picture of something that you hold in your mind.
examples: The appearance of the town in her memory did not match the real place.

oewn-01236192-n.learner: The formal act of someone who is part of a legal case coming to a court or a hearing.
examples: The accused man made his first appearance in court on Monday.

oewn-00949109-v.learner: To decide on something, or to fix it clearly and for certain.
examples: We still have to determine the price of the tickets.

oewn-00701581-v.learner: To fix something so that it is final, or to fix it as someone with the power to do so.
examples: The party then gathered round the fire to hear Lady Catherine determine what weather they were to have on the morrow.

oewn-00922307-v.learner: To find out or learn something for certain, usually by asking or by making some other effort.
examples: Call the station to determine whether the train is on time.

oewn-00702474-v.learner: To set how far something reaches, or to set its limits.
examples: The contract determines exactly which rooms the builder will work on.

oewn-00765444-v.learner: To settle something so that it is final, or to reach an agreement.
examples: The two sides met to determine the quarrel over the land.

oewn-05840588-n.learner: Something or someone that makes you worried, or that makes you unhappy.
examples: Her son's poor health was a constant concern.

oewn-08077878-n.learner: A business or factory, together with the people who make it up.
examples: He ran a small printing concern in the town.

oewn-06632357-n.learner: A programme about things happening now, often with interviews and people giving their views.
examples: We watch the news every night at seven.

oewn-05200165-n.learner: The quality of being interesting enough to be reported in news reports.
examples: Once the scandal faded, he was no longer news.
